proposals.before: During Qianning the Founder besieged Yan; Zhu Xuan begged Taiyuan for help.
proposals.after: During Qianning the Founder pressed the attack on Yan and Yun; Zhu Xuan begged Taiyuan for help.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops 鄆 (Yun) from 兗、鄆, collapsing two war theaters into Yan alone.

proposals.before: In Qianning, the Founder pressed the attack on Yan and Yanzhou; Zhu Xuan sought aid from Taiyuan.
proposals.after: In Qianning, the Founder pressed the attack on Yan and Yunzhou; Zhu Xuan sought aid from Taiyuan.
proposals.reason: 鄆 is Yunzhou, not a second Yanzhou; 兗 already supplies Yan.

proposals.before: Hongxin beheaded Luoluo and the Jin army withdrew.
proposals.after: The Founder had him sent to Hongxin, who beheaded him, and the Jin army then withdrew.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits 太祖令送於宏信, the Founder's order that Luoluo be delivered to Hongxin before the beheading.

proposals.before: While attacking Yan the Founder courted Hongxin yearly with humble, lavish gifts lest Wei turn away.
proposals.after: While planning against Yan and Yun the Founder courted Hongxin yearly with humble, lavish gifts lest Wei turn away.
proposals.reason: Chinese 方圖兗、鄆 names both Yan and Yun; idiomatic keeps only Yan.

proposals.before: At that time the Founder was planning Yan and Yanzhou and feared Hongxin would turn aside; each year's seasonal gifts were sure to use humble words and rich courtesy.
proposals.after: At that time the Founder was planning Yan and Yunzhou and feared Hongxin would turn aside; each year's seasonal gifts were sure to use humble words and rich courtesy.
proposals.reason: 鄆 is Yunzhou, not Yanzhou.

proposals.before: (The 《Old Book of Tang》 records steady promotion from Wende through Qianning.)〉
proposals.after: (The Old Book of Tang: from the start of Wende Shaowei was appointed Left Regular Cavalry Attendant and deputy military commissioner of Tianxiong; from Longji to Qianning, in ten years, he repeatedly received offices and titles.)
proposals.reason: Idiomatic erases the named offices and the Longji–Qianning span, and keeps a stray annotation closer.

proposals.before: They installed every commander—Shi Xianzheng, He Quanhan, Han Junxiong, Le Yanzhen among them.
proposals.after: They installed every commander—Shi Xiancheng, He Quanhao, Han Junxiong, and Le Yanzhen among them.
proposals.reason: 憲誠 is Xiancheng, not Xianzheng; 皞 is Hao, not Han.

proposals.before: Commanders' removal and installation came from their hands—men like Shi Xianzheng, He Quanhan, Han Junxiong, and Le Yanzhen were all set up by them.
proposals.after: Commanders' removal and installation came from their hands—men like Shi Xiancheng, He Quanhao, Han Junxiong, and Le Yanzhen were all set up by them.
proposals.reason: Same name errors as the idiomatic line: 誠 and 皞 are mistranscribed.

proposals.before: Court mourned three days and posthumously made him Minister of Works.
proposals.after: Court mourned three days and posthumously made him Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
proposals.reason: 尚書令 is the Director of the Department of State Affairs, not 司空/工部 Minister of Works.

proposals.before: (The 《Taiping Era》 cites his biography: among frontier lords he was most praised for writing.
proposals.after: (The 《Extensive Records of the Taiping Era》 cites his biography: among frontier lords he was most praised for writing.
proposals.reason: 太平廣記 is the book title Taiping Guangji, not a bare era name.

proposals.before: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 supplement cites Zhouhan's rapid rise to Wei commissioner.)〉
proposals.after: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian Kaoyi》 cites the 《Biographies of Liang Merit Ministers》: Zhouhan was restored as Cloud-Banner General and acting Tianxiong commissioner, soon honorary Situ, then formally Wei-Bo commissioner.)〉
proposals.reason: The note names 梁功臣傳 and offices 雲麾將軍、節度留後、檢校司徒; 司徒 is not Minister of Works, and the idiomatic line drops those ranks.

proposals.before: For generations they served Zhongwu; Bin, Yingqi, and Shuwen held the family posts.
proposals.after: For generations they were Zhongwu guard officers; great-grandfather Bin, grandfather Yingqi, and father Shuwen all held the old posts.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops 牙將 and the kinship ranks 曾祖/祖/父 that the Chinese and literal supply.

proposals.before: Within two li of the gates all grain was brought inside the city.
proposals.after: Outside all four gates, within two stages, people with grain were all ordered to haul it into the prefectural city.
proposals.reason: 兩舍 is two staging distances (classically thirty li each), not two li; the idiomatic rendering invents a false measure.

proposals.before: Brothers Chang and Gui commanded defense and guard; sons Lu and Lin led elite troops.
proposals.after: He made his second brother Chang defense commander and his youngest brother Xu personal-guard commander of horse and army; eldest son Lu and second son Lin each led crack troops.
proposals.reason: 珝 is Xu, not Gui; the idiomatic line also flattens the distinct offices 防遏都指揮使 and 親從都知兵馬使.

proposals.before: He made his second brother Chang defense commander, his youngest brother Gui personal guard commander of horse and army; eldest son Lu and second son Lin each led crack troops.
proposals.after: He made his second brother Chang defense commander, his youngest brother Xu personal guard commander of horse and army; eldest son Lu and second son Lin each led crack troops.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise mistranscribes 珝 as Gui.

proposals.before: Soon he became Grand Marshal and Earl of Yingchuan.
proposals.after: Within months he was made Minister of Works (Sikong) and advanced to Earl of Yingchuan.
proposals.reason: 司空 is Minister of Works, not Grand Marshal (太尉); the same chapter later uses 太尉 correctly for the posthumous honor.

proposals.before: Wende 1 Cai fell; the court made Chou honorary Minister of Works, Taining commissioner, then Zhexi commissioner while remaining at Wankiu.
proposals.after: In Wende year 1 Cai was pacified; the court discussed merit and made Chou honorary Situ and Taining military commissioner, then reassigned him Zhexi military commissioner without leaving Wankiu, holding both commands.
proposals.reason: Chinese 檢校司徒 is honorary Situ, not Minister of Works (司空).

proposals.before: Eldest son Lu rose to chief minister rank.
proposals.after: Eldest son Lu rose to the ranked ministers.
proposals.reason: 列卿 means the listed/nine ministers, not the chief-minister (宰相) rank.

proposals.before: The eldest son Lu reached the rank of chief minister.
proposals.after: The eldest son Lu reached the rank of the listed ministers.
proposals.reason: 列卿 is the ranked ministers, not chief minister.

proposals.before: Chou made Chang Taizhou prefect and honorary Right Vice Director.
proposals.after: When Chou held the Taining military commission at a distance, he made Chang prefect of this prefecture and honorary Right Vice Director.
proposals.reason: 本州 is this prefecture (Chen), not Taizhou; 泰寧 is the Taining command Chou held remotely.

proposals.before: Month 7, year 3, he governed Su prefecture, then Yi prefecture.
proposals.after: Month 7, year 3, he governed Su prefecture, then was transferred as prefect.
proposals.reason: 旋移州刺史 means he was soon transferred to a prefectship; 移 is the verb 'transfer', not the place Yi.

proposals.before: In the seventh month of year 3 he went out as regimental commissioner of Su prefecture; soon he was prefect of Yi prefecture.
proposals.after: In the seventh month of year 3 he went out as regimental commissioner of Su prefecture; soon he was transferred to be prefect.
proposals.reason: 移刺史 is transfer to prefect, not prefect of Yi prefecture.

proposals.before: Grown, he excelled at archery and the 《Three Strategies》.
proposals.after: When grown, he excelled at mounted archery and was especially versed in the Three Strategies.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic drops 騎 from 騎射 (mounted archery) and keeps Chinese book-title brackets in English.

proposals.before: After Chou's death Gui became campaign deputy under Chang.
proposals.after: When Chou died, Chang was Zhongwu military commissioner; Gui was transferred to campaign deputy and honorary Sikong.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits Chang holding Zhongwu and Gui's 檢校司空.

proposals.before: Soon he was Grand Marshal and full Zhongwu commissioner.
proposals.after: Soon he was Specially Advanced and honorary Minister of Works (Situ), and full Zhongwu military commissioner.
proposals.reason: 特進、檢校司徒 is Specially Advanced and honorary Situ, not Grand Marshal.

proposals.before: For twenty years the Zhao brothers ruled Chen and Xu and won the people's love.
proposals.after: For more than twenty years the Gui brothers controlled Chen and Xu and won the Chen people's love.
proposals.reason: Source has 珝兄弟, not the surname Zhao, and 二十餘年 is more than twenty years.

proposals.before: Tianfu 1 winter Han Jian summoned Gui to Tongzhou as acting Kuangguo commissioner.
proposals.after: In winter of Tianfu 1, Han Jian was Zhongwu military commissioner and then summoned Gui to Tongzhou as acting Kuangguo commissioner.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits 韓建為忠武軍節度使, the office from which the transfer was made.

proposals.before: When the emperor returned to Chang'an, Gui was summoned and honored as Welcoming-the-Carriage merit minister.
proposals.after: Soon Zhaozong returned to Chang'an; an edict summoned him to audience and granted the title Merit Minister Welcoming the Imperial Carriage.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic replaces named 昭宗 with 'the emperor' and omits the edict and audience.

proposals.before: Wang Ke came from Hedong.
proposals.after: Wang Ke came from Hezhong.
proposals.reason: Chinese 河中 names Hezhong, not Hedong (河東).

proposals.before: Wang Ke was a Hedong man.
proposals.after: Wang Ke was a Hezhong man.
proposals.reason: Chinese 河中 names Hezhong, not Hedong (河東).

proposals.before: Guangqi 3 Chongrong was killed; Chongying took Pu and made Ke deputy.
proposals.after: In Guangqi 3 of Tang Xizong, Chongrong was killed by his officer Chang Xingru; they pushed Chongrong's younger brother Chongying as Pu commander and made Ke campaign deputy.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic drops Emperor Xizong, the killer Chang Xingru, and Chongying's stated younger-brother relation.

proposals.before: Tianfu 1 spring Cunjing seized Jin and Jiang and blocked Taiyuan relief at Jinzhou.
proposals.after: In spring of Tianfu 1, Cunjing's troops took Jin and Jiang and ordered He Yinsi to hold Jin Prefecture to choke Taiyuan relief.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits 何糸因, who was ordered to hold Jinzhou.

proposals.before: Besieged, Ke's wife wrote Keyong, "We will soon be prisoners begging food at Daliang—how can you not save us!"
proposals.after: In the second month, as the great army pressed Hezhong, Ke's wife wrote to Taiyuan: "The enemy presses hard; soon we will be captives begging food at Daliang—how can you bear not to save us!"
proposals.reason: Idiomatic replaces 太原 with Keyong and drops the month and Hezhong setting.

proposals.before: Ke offered to surrender bound with a sheep; the Founder said, "How can I forget Grand Marshal Chongrong's grace! If you meet me with a lost-state rite, what will the yellow springs say of me!"
proposals.after: Ke offered to present himself bound, leading a sheep; the Founder said, "How can I forget the Grand Preceptor and maternal uncle's grace! If you, sir, meet me with a lost-state rite, what will the yellow springs say of me!"
proposals.reason: 太師 is Grand Preceptor, 阿舅 is maternal uncle, and this sentence does not name Chongrong.

proposals.before: The historian asks: Shaowei aided Liang's usurpation—hero to Liang, traitor to Tang?
proposals.after: The historian says: Shaowei at first was a Tang hero and held the Wei region; in the Tang house's last years he urged the Liang Founder toward a forced abdication. In Liang he was a minister who helped found the mandate; in Tang, could he be called a loyal minister?
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English omits holding Wei, the Tang house's declining fortune, urging the Liang Founder to a forced abdication, and the founding-aide versus loyal-minister contrast.

proposals.before: Zhao Chou held tiny Chen against Chao's millions—his defense deserves praise.
proposals.after: Zhao Chou, with only the tiny territory of Huaiyang, resisted Huang Chao's million-strong host; his merit and accomplishment deserve much praise.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English replaces Huaiyang with Chen and shortens Huang Chao to Chao, obscuring the named place and person of the Chinese.

decisions.reason: The Chinese 急攻兗、鄆 names a pressed attack on both Yan and Yun; the original English keeps only Yan and turns the attack into a siege.
兗 is already Yan; 鄆 is Yunzhou, so the literal's second Yanzhou is a false duplicate of Yan.
The sentence opens 太祖令送於宏信; the original English omits the Founder's order that Luoluo be delivered to Hongxin before the beheading.
方圖兗、鄆 is planning against Yan and Yun, not attacking Yan alone.
鄆 is Yunzhou, not Yanzhou; the literal repeats the same false doubling of Yan.
The Old Book of Tang note names 左散騎常侍, 天雄軍節度副使, and promotions 自龍紀至乾寧，十年之中, all erased in the original English.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 紹威自文德初授左散騎常侍，充天雄軍節度副使，自龍紀至乾寧，十年之中，累加官爵

decisions.reason: 史憲誠 is Xiancheng and 何全皞 is Quanhao; the original English misreads 誠 and 皞.
The literal line has the same 憲誠/Xiancheng and 皞/Hao errors as the idiomatic.
冊贈尚書令 is a posthumous Shangshu ling, not 司空 Minister of Works.
太平廣記 is the book Taiping Guangji, not the era name Taiping alone.
The note cites 通鑒考異引《梁功臣傳》 and lists 雲麾將軍, 節度留後, and 檢校司徒, all dropped in the original English.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 《通鑒考異》引《梁功臣傳》云：周翰起復雲麾將軍，充天雄軍節度留後，尋檢校司徒

decisions.reason: 代為忠武牙將 and 曾祖賓，祖英奇，父叔文 name a guard-officer line and three kinship ranks omitted in the original English.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 代為忠武牙將，曾祖賓，祖英奇，父叔文

decisions.reason: 兩舍 is two staging distances, not two li; the original also drops 四門之外 and 民有資糧者.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 凡四門之外，兩舍之內，民有資糧者

decisions.reason: 珝 is Xu, not Gui, and 防遏都指揮使 and 親從都知兵馬使 are distinct offices flattened in the original.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以仲弟昶為防遏都指揮使，以季弟珝為親從都知兵馬使

decisions.reason: The literal likewise transcribes 珝 as Gui.
加司空 is Sikong, Minister of Works, not Grand Marshal 太尉.
檢校司徒 is honorary Situ, not 司空; the line also records 朝廷議勳 and 兼領二鎮.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以犨檢校司徒，充泰寧軍節度使

decisions.reason: 列卿 is the ranked or listed ministers, not chief-minister 宰相 rank.
The literal likewise renders 列卿 as chief minister.
本州 is this prefecture, not Taizhou; 遙領泰寧軍節度 is Chou's distant Taining command.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 犨遙領泰寧軍節度，以昶為本州刺史

decisions.reason: 旋移州刺史 uses 移 as the verb transfer, not a place named Yi.
The literal likewise takes 移 as the prefecture Yi.
工騎射 is mounted archery and 尤精《三略》 marks special command of that work; the original drops 騎 and keeps Chinese brackets.

decisions.after: When Chou died, Chang was Zhongwu military commissioner; Xu was transferred to campaign deputy and honorary Sikong.
decisions.reason: The original omits 昶為忠武軍節度使 and 檢校司空, but the proposal still calls 珝 Gui; the corrected English uses Xu.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 昶為忠武軍節度使，珝遷為行軍司馬、檢校司空

decisions.after: Soon he was Specially Advanced and honorary Situ, and full Zhongwu military commissioner.
decisions.reason: 特進、檢校司徒 is Specially Advanced and honorary Situ, not Grand Marshal; the proposal wrongly glosses Situ as Minister of Works (司空).

decisions.after: For more than twenty years Xu and his brothers controlled Chen and Xu and won the Chen people's love.
decisions.reason: 二十餘年 and 陳人 are in the source, but replacing Zhao with Gui keeps the 珝 mistranscription; the Chinese is 珝兄弟, Xu and his brothers.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 珝兄弟節制陳、許，繼擁旌鉞，共二十餘年，陳人愛戴

decisions.after: In winter of Tianfu 1, Han Jian was Zhongwu military commissioner and then summoned Xu to Tongzhou as acting Kuangguo commissioner.
decisions.reason: 韓建為忠武軍節度使 is omitted in the original, but the proposal still names 珝 as Gui.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 韓建為忠武軍節度使，乃征珝知同州匡國軍節度留後

decisions.reason: The Chinese names 昭宗, 詔征入覲, and the title 迎鑾功臣, all reduced in the original English.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 俄而昭宗還長安，詔征入覲，錫迎鑾功臣之號

decisions.reason: 河中 is Hezhong; Hedong is 河東, used later of Chongrong's office, not of Ke's native place.
The literal likewise renders 河中 as Hedong.
The original drops 唐僖宗, the killer 常行儒, and 重榮弟, all explicit in the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 唐僖宗光啟三年，重榮為部將常行儒所害，推重榮弟重盈為蒲帥

decisions.reason: 令何糸因守晉州 names He Yinsi as the officer holding Jin to choke Taiyuan relief.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 令何糸因守晉州以扼太原援師

decisions.reason: The letter is 書告太原 in the second month as 大軍逼河中; the original substitutes Keyong and drops the setting.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 二月，大軍逼河中，珂妻書告太原曰

decisions.after: Ke offered to present himself bound, leading a sheep; the Founder said, "How can I forget the grace of my maternal uncle the Grand Preceptor! If you, sir, meet me with a lost-state rite, what will the yellow springs say of me!"
decisions.reason: 太師阿舅 is one person, the Grand Preceptor as maternal uncle, not Grand Marshal Chongrong; the proposal's "and" can split them into two.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 太師阿舅之恩，何時可忘

decisions.reason: 史臣曰 records holding Wei, 土德之季運, 倡梁祖以強禪, and the 佐命 versus 忠臣 contrast, all missing from the original.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 紹威始為唐雄，據魏地，當土德之季運，倡梁祖以強禪，在梁則為佐命也，在唐則豈得為忠臣乎

decisions.reason: The comment names 淮陽 and 黃巢, not Chen and Chao.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 趙犨以淮陽咫尺之地，抗黃巢百萬之眾

claimRevisions.reason: The English personal name Shi Xianzheng was produced by misreading 誠; the source is 史憲誠.
The extracted given-name English Xianzheng contradicts 誠 and the claim's own pinyin Xiancheng.
The English personal name He Quanhan was produced by misreading 皞; the source is 何全皞.
The extracted given-name English Quanhan contradicts 皞 and the claim's own pinyin Quanhao.
The English given name Gui was produced by the bad transcription of 珝; pinyin already has Xu.
The kinship label repeats the Gui mistranscription of 珝.
檢校司徒 is honorary Situ, not 司空 Minister of Works; the English office label followed the same confusion as the translation.
